bib.title: Memory Transfer Learning: How Memories are Transferred Across Domains in Coding Agents

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Memory Transfer Learning: How Memories are Transferred Across Domains in Coding Agents", Kangsan Kim, Minki Kang, Taeil Kim, Yanlai Yang, Mengye Ren, Sung Ju Hwang (KAIST, NYU, DeepAuto.ai). arXiv 2604.14004v1, 15 Apr 2026. Preprint: the PDF names no venue, though it uses ICML-style formatting. The file is /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/03-agentic-foundations/sources/kim-2026-memory-transfer-learning.pdf.

COVERAGE: All 73,725 chars were read. That covers the main text, Tables 1-10, the appendices (A Pass@1, B negative transfer, C formal model, D categories, E generation prompts) and the reference list. I skimmed the references only for origins. The paper has no separate limitations section.

CLAIMS (ranked)

1. Abstraction predicts transfer. Insight scores best, Summary next, then Workflow, with Trajectory worst. Every format beats zero-shot on average, but Trajectory's gain is small and it hurts on some benchmarks.
 - number: GPT-5-mini average Pass@3 is 0.523 zero-shot, 0.534 Trajectory (T), 0.538 Workflow (W), 0.546 Summary (S), 0.560 Insight (I). The gain is +3.7 points for Insight.
 - setup: Pool is memories from all other benchmarks, leaving out the test benchmark. 6 benchmarks (LiveCodeBench v6, Aider-Polyglot, SWE-Bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2, ReplicationBench, MLGym). At most 100 tasks per benchmark. Pass@3. gpt-5-mini is the agent, memory generator and judge. mini-swe-agent. Top-3 retrieval by embedding. Trajectory memory also scores below zero-shot on TerminalBench2 (0.270 vs 0.315) and MLGym (0.583 vs 0.667).
 - quote: "MTL (T) 0.940 0.490 0.770 0.270 0.122 0.583 0.534" and "MTL (I) 0.930 0.470 0.770 0.360 0.189 0.7500.560"
 - where: Table 1, p5.

2. What transfers is meta-knowledge (inspect, edit, verify, submit; self-made tests; environment guardrails). Task-specific algorithm content barely transfers.
 - number: Algorithmic Strategy Transfer is 5.5% of gains.
 - setup: Cases that failed zero-shot and passed with Insight memory, categorised by GPT-5 into 10 classes. Figure 3 lists the shares as percentages (14.5, 15.0, 14.4, 10.4, 5.5, 6.4, 7.8, 8.1, 8.5, 9.5). The extraction does not tie each share to its label, apart from the 5.5%.
 - quote: "Algorithmic Strategy Transfer accounts for only 5.5% of the total gains in Figure 3, suggesting that the direct transfer of specific programming knowledge or algorithms is limited in our setting."
 - where: Sec 4.2.1, p6.

3. Within one format (Insight), the task-agnostic memories beat the task-specific ones by a small margin.
 - number: +1.1 points on average (0.523 vs 0.534).
 - setup: The top 30% and bottom 30% of Insights are split by how well an LLM can recover the original task from the memory alone. 3 benchmarks (LCB, SWEB, RepliB). The gaps are small, with no variance or significance test.
 - quote: "Task-specific Insights 0.887 0.617 0.067 0.523 / Task-agnostic Insights 0.893 0.627 0.0820.534"
 - where: Table 4, p7.

4. A small cross-domain pool beats larger or in-domain-only memory systems, but only on 3 benchmarks.
 - number: MTL (I) scores 0.630 average with 431 memories. ReasoningBank scores 0.601 with 97 memories. AgentKB scores 0.613 with 5,899 memories. Zero-shot scores 0.584.
 - setup: LCB, SWEB and ReplicationBench only. Pass@3.
 - quote: "MTL (Ours) 431 0.930 0.770 0.1890.630"
 - where: Table 2, p5.

5. Negative transfer happens through three paths: domain-mismatched anchoring, false validation confidence, and misapplied best-practice transfer. A Trajectory memory acted as a "brittle anchor" (an sklearn `sparse=` argument error carried over from MLGym). A Workflow memory carried an R heredoc pattern into a C++ task.
 - number: none
 - setup: Qualitative cases from an LLM categorisation and from Appendix B. Insight memory was also bent into a "quick completion" excuse.
 - quote: "the transferred Trajectory memory acts as a brittle anchor, leading the agent to execute incompatible commands and ultimately causing runtime errors."
 - where: Sec 4.3.4 p7, Sec 4.4.1 p8, Table 9.

6. Simple embedding retrieval beat LLM reranking and LLM rewriting of memories.
 - number: Average Pass@3 is 0.630 for embedding, 0.608 for adaptive rewriting, 0.598 for LLM reranking, and 0.584 for no memory.
 - setup: LCB, SWEB, RepliB only. Reranking takes 20 candidates and the LLM picks 3.
 - quote: "Adaptive Rewriting 0.920 0.760 0.144 0.608 / Embedding Similarity 0.930 0.770 0.1890.630"
 - where: Table 7, p9.

7. Gains scale with pool size and number of source domains, and memories transfer across models. Self-generated memories are still best.
 - number: Cross-model Pass@1 average is 0.543 for GPT-5-mini with its own memories, 0.528 with Qwen3-Coder memories, 0.518 with DeepSeek memories, against 0.515 zero-shot.
 - setup: The scaling result is only in Figure 6, with no numbers in the text. The cross-model figures are on 3 benchmarks (Table 6).
 - quote: "GPT-5-mini GPT-5-mini 0.877 0.633 0.119 0.543" and "Zeroshot GPT-5-mini 0.863 0.623 0.059 0.515"
 - where: Table 6, p9.

LIMITS
- Single paper, with the agent, judge and memory writer all gpt-5-mini. Other models (DeepSeek V3.2, Qwen3-Coder) were run with Insight only.
- Benchmarks are subsampled to 100 tasks and several are small. Most per-benchmark gains are 1-8 points on a small n, and no confidence intervals or seeds are given for Table 1. Table 2 mentions three runs.
- Reported "%" deltas are absolute points. Several are 0.0 or negative. Aider fell -1.0 points for DeepSeek, and Qwen is flat on two benchmarks.
- The memory pool is a one-off offline batch, not an online accumulating memory. Memories are created from an LLM judge's success or fail call.
- The abstraction claim rests on four formats that also differ in length and prompt. The only controlled test is Table 4, a small effect. Appendix C's "Proposition 1" is a toy model under stated assumptions, not evidence. The text calls it "proves".
- The authors concede that static retrieval does not fit multi-step settings and suggest step-wise retrieval and domain routing. Negative transfer is not solved.
- This paper has no skill-library or executable-skill condition, so it does not compare insights with skills. "Workflow" here is a short list of bash commands, as in AWM.
- Only coding agents. The cross-model result is on a few models.

BUILDS ON
- Formats: Trajectory (Zheng et al., 2024, per the text), Workflow (Wang et al., 2024c, Agent Workflow Memory), Summary (Shinn et al., 2023, Reflexion), Insight (Ouyang et al., 2025, ReasoningBank, arXiv 2509.25140).
- Compared against: AgentKB (Tang et al., 2025), ReasoningBank.
- Also cited: Dynamic Cheatsheet (Suzgun et al., 2025), ReMe (Cao et al., 2025), MemEvolve (Zhang et al., 2025), Memp (Fang et al., 2025b), mini-swe-agent (Yang et al., 2024), harbor (Team, 2026).
- Benchmarks: SWE-bench (Jimenez et al., ICLR 2024), LiveCodeBench (Jain et al., 2024), Terminal-Bench (Merrill et al., 2026), MLGym (Nathani et al., 2025).

CODE: None in the body. The Insight memory schema, from the Figure 11 prompt, is JSON `{"title": ..., "description": ..., "content": "1-3 sentences describing the insights learned..."}`. The prompt rules are "You can extract only one memory item from the trajectory" and "Do not mention specific files or details, but rather focus on the generalizable insights." The Insight prompt is at p19 and the Workflow, Summary and Insight prompts for success and failure cases are in Figs 7-12, pp16-19.

FIGURES
- Figure 2 (p3): "Illustrative examples of four memory formats" (Trajectory, Workflow, Summary, Insight) as a ladder of abstraction. It is the single best candidate, because it shows the raw-to-distilled spectrum that the chapter's comparison needs. I could not render it. The extraction shows only its text labels.
- Figure 3 (p6): the breakdown of the contribution categories, which supports claim 2.
- Figure 6 (p9): scaling with pool size and number of domains.

PROBLEMS: Nothing garbled except in Figure 3, where the labels and percentages cannot be matched up. No embedded instructions found. I did not view the figure images. Tables 1 and 2 are copied from the extraction, where the best value runs into the Avg column (for example "0.7500.560").
